title.value: Common limitations of performance metrics in biomedical image analysis
title.justification: The title 'Common limitations of performance metrics in biomedical image analysis' succinctly captures the central theme of the paper, which discusses the pitfalls of widely used performance metrics in biomedical image analysis.
title.quote: Common limitations of performance metrics in biomedical image analysis

analysis.description: This paper discusses the limitations and pitfalls of commonly used performance metrics, specifically the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), in the context of biomedical image analysis. It highlights issues regarding the mathematical properties, task suitability, and metric aggregation in segmentation tasks.

type.justification: The paper analyzes performance metrics from a theoretical perspective, discussing their limitations and potential improvements rather than conducting empirical experiments.
type.quote: While the importance of automatic biomedical image analysis is increasing at an enormous pace, recent meta-research revealed major flaws with respect to algorithm validation. Performance metrics are key for objective, transparent and comparative performance assessment, but little attention has been given to their pitfalls.

name.justification: The paper primarily addresses the domain of biomedical image analysis, focusing on the performance assessment metrics used in this field.
name.quote: Performance metrics are key for objective, transparent and comparative performance assessment, but little attention has been given to their pitfalls.

name.justification: The paper specifically addresses segmentation tasks within biomedical image analysis, particularly analyzing metrics used for segmentation.
name.quote: Image segmentation is one of the most popular image processing tasks.

name.justification: The paper discusses the validation of performance metrics themselves, which is a significant aspect of ensuring the correctness of biomedical image analysis results.
name.quote: Our MIDL presentation raises awareness about some common flaws of the most frequently used segmentation metric in the biomedical image analysis community.
